subject: Whistic snapshot refresh automation & CAIQ delta mapping
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.h@redwood.com>
To: Samir Tan <vendor-ops@whistic.com>, Lena Park <lena.park@clearviewsecurity.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.m@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.w@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Whistic snapshot refresh automation & CAIQ delta mapping

Hi Samir / Lena,

Following up from our intake call last week — ClearView would like a regular, machine-consumable snapshot of their Whistic profile (every 30 days) plus a small delta feed for CAIQ/SIG field changes so we can keep our public-facing security page and audit artifacts in sync. Attached is a sample CSV with the fields we currently consume.

High-level asks from our side:
- Scheduled snapshots (zip of signed evidence + canonical JSON manifest) delivered via webhook or SFTP.
- A delta feed (list of changed fields + timestamp + proof_of_possession refs) for CAIQ mapping so our bot can re-evaluate downstream alerts.
- Recommended field names from Whistic for CAIQ/SIG equivalence (we'll map locally but want to avoid fragile name matching).
- API key / webhook auth guidance and rate limits.

Attaching: whistic-refresh-proposal.csv (sample manifest), caiq-sig-field-mapping-draft.xlsx (our starting mapping).

Can you confirm whether Whistic supports:
1) scheduled snapshot zips with signed artifacts,
2) a delta webhook for profile field changes, and
3) an HMAC-signed webhook payload (we prefer HMAC over basic auth).

If Whistic has a standard payload schema for delta events, please paste an example in your reply — that will speed our implementation.

Thanks,
Mina
Mina Haddad
Security Intake Lead, Redwood Inference
mina.h@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0132

---

Attachment: caiq-sig-field-mapping-draft.xlsx
From: Samir Tan <vendor-ops@whistic.com>

Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Whistic snapshot refresh automation & CAIQ delta mapping

Hi Mina — thanks for the clear notes and the sample files. We can support the requested flows; short answers up front:

1) Scheduled snapshots: yes — we can package a profile zip containing a JSON manifest + evidence files. We can sign the manifest using a Whistic-signed SHA256 signature and include a signature.txt inside the zip.

2) Delta feed: we offer an events webhook for profile edits. The payload includes changed_fields (array), changed_by (user/email), and a change_timestamp. We can add a proof_of_possession reference (signed_evidence_id) that points to the snapshot S3 key.

3) Auth: HMAC is supported on webhooks (X-Whistic-Signature). Our API rate limit for profile export is 60 requests/min for paid portal customers; bulk snapshot ops can be done via our SFTP batch endpoint for larger archives.

Example delta webhook payload (trimmed):
{
  "profile_id": "pv_8f3a...",
  "changed_fields": ["network_security.tls_versions", "data_retention.policy_days"],
  "signed_evidence_id": "evidence_20270409_23.zip",
  "change_timestamp": "2027-04-09T17:02:12Z"
}

I'll also attach our lightweight mapping doc and a short spec for webhook HMAC signatures. For the scheduled snapshot, we prefer SFTP delivery for large attachments but webhook + presign link is fine for ~<200MB.

Next steps:
- Samir: I'll drop the mapping doc and the HMAC spec in my next message.
- Mina / Rishi: confirm whether you want SFTP or webhook presign to be the primary delivery.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Tan
Partner Ops, Whistic
vendor-ops@whistic.com

Attachment: whistic-webhook-hmac-spec.txt (small)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.m@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.h@redwood.com>, Samir Tan <vendor-ops@whistic.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 12:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Whistic snapshot refresh automation & CAIQ delta mapping

Thanks Samir. Quick internal notes:
- We need the signed evidence to include a KMS-wrapped checksum / manifest reference for audit. If Whistic's signature is separate, we should still compute and store our own hash (SHA256) and store it in our proof store.
- TTL: prefer 30-day snapshot cadence, but keep one full 12-month archive retained for compliance.
- For delta events, please include the pre and post value for changed fields where possible — this helps our regression evals and alerting.

Mina: Jonas and I are fine with webhook presigns for small files but would lean SFTP for full monthly zips >200MB. Jonas — flag if you disagree.

-rishi
From: Samir Tan <vendor-ops@whistic.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.m@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.h@redwood.com>
Cc: Lena Park <lena.park@clearviewsecurity.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 15:36:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Whistic snapshot refresh automation & CAIQ delta mapping

Thanks for the details, Rishi. We can include pre_value and post_value in webhook payloads for field-level edits — we'll add a small size warning when diffs exceed 4KB for a single field (large binary blobs will be comprised as signed_evidence references).

For the KMS-wrapped checksum, we don't expose our private key material, but we will include a Whistic-signed SHA256 of the manifest and provide an S3 presign for the evidence zip. You're correct to compute and keep your own hash on ingestion.

I'll draft a sample manifest that contains: profile_id, manifest_sha256, evidence_files (name + s3_key), created_at, whistic_signature, and an optional kms_reference for customers on enterprise plans.

Will send the manifest draft Monday; in the meantime, can you confirm the SFTP username format and whether ClearView wants a PST-based delivery window?

- Samir
From: Mina Haddad <mina.h@redwood.com>
To: Samir Tan <vendor-ops@whistic.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.m@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.w@redwood.com>, Lena Park <lena.park@clearviewsecurity.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Whistic snapshot refresh automation & CAIQ delta mapping

Samir — thank you. Confirming our implementation preferences and a couple of clarifying asks: 

1) Delivery preference: primary = webhook presign for <200MB; fallback = SFTP for monthly full zips.
2) Retention: Redwood will keep a rolling 30-day snapshot and one 12-month cold archive copy for audits; please include manifest_sha256 in every snapshot so we can assert proof_of_possession.
3) Webhook security: HMAC header name acceptable (X-Whistic-Signature). We'll validate and rotate our webhook secret quarterly.

Clarifying asks for the manifest draft you mentioned: please include explicit keys we can map to CAIQ/SIG categories (e.g., network_security.tls_versions, auth.mfa_enforced, data_retention.policy_days). If Whistic exposes nested keys as dotted paths, we'll consume them directly; otherwise please provide canonical names.

Jonas, Rishi: can you confirm we have bandwidth to implement the webhook consumer and presign ingestion before May 14? If not, we'll propose a shorter POC with manual handoffs.

Thanks — Mina
From: Lena Park <lena.park@clearviewsecurity.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.h@redwood.com>, Samir Tan <vendor-ops@whistic.com>

Appreciate the fast answers. ClearView prefers webhook presign flow for the POC; if everything looks clean we'll move to scheduled SFTP delivery for full monthly zips. Two additional asks from procurement/security:

- The snapshot must include a signed manifest and a machine-readable listing of evidence types (e.g., config_dump.json, s3_presign.txt, sso_assertion.jwt).
- We need a DocuSign link (or equivalent) for the data transfer addendum before enabling automated SFTP drops. Can Whistic provide the DTA template or should ClearView generate it?

Samir — can you confirm who on your team will share the DocuSign and the SFTP username conventions?

Thanks,
Lena Park
